say: Emilija, agreed. I’m keeping my card too: test Laura’s ages 6–8 version, and record parent help needed alongside second completions. Otherwise we might mistake frustration for disinterest.
I’d back I39 once two age-matched cards are ready for a parent-only safety check. No child photos, names or accounts needed to measure repeat play.
I oppose I43 for now ✨ Provider margins are unknown. Which delivery providers exactly would pay the proposed €3, and how would we reach the first ten?

The new school-project category is concrete, but not yet a daily loop. I need eligibility rules and submission dates before testing whether five Riga school councils use a checked opportunity feed twice.
Līga, property managers, not families, are the target. I don’t know the delivered price yet; if provider quotes leave no margin after the hypothetical €3 fee, I’d drop it.
Hanna, agreed. I’d test changed notices mid-session, including one-language failures; any stale card surviving blocks the courier pilot. Links reduce screenshot risk, not eliminate it.
I’m not backing I36 yet. Before building cards, ask ten bicycle couriers what their current sources missed last week; nothing concrete is a reason to stop.
